column3: Split-flap departure board. A 256x64 Solari board in a station hall: the time is the board itself, a row of big split-flap modules (real flaps with a hinge line, the top half lit from above, the bottom half in shade, printed numerals in a classic railway face designed for this grid), plus the departure rows the banner allows (destinations, platforms, a frog-themed train name, 'ON TIME'). Always alive: the station clock's seconds module ticks, a stray flap occasionally re-seats, passengers' shadows pass, a pigeon walks the top edge. Minute turn: the changing module flips through every intermediate flap with real 3D rotation (perspective foreshortening, motion blur, the flap's back showing, a little bounce as it lands), rattling in cascade; the time is never wrong because only one numeral is ever fully seated. Hour: the whole board refreshes left to right in a rolling wave of flaps, rows scrolling up as trains depart. The physical, clattering flip is the point.

Roller coaster. A 192x64 panorama of a funfair at dusk: the time IS the coaster track. Four digits drawn as one continuous steel track with a lattice of supports, with loops for 0, 6, 8 and 9, drops and camelbacks for the rest (design track letterforms). A train of cars (the owner's rainbow frog in round glasses in the front car, arms up) rides the whole track all the time with real physics: speed from energy conservation, slow on the crests, fast in the dips, cars banking and following the curve, a chain lift clanking it up. Fairground lights chase along the rails. Minute turn: the changing digit's track flexes like a spline into the new digit while the train waits on the lift hill (it never derails, and the track never reads as another number). Hour: a launch, the train screams through every loop with fireworks. A ride the owner would watch.

Beanstalk. A 64x192 tower: a magic vine climbs from a pot at the bottom to the clouds at the top. The time is written by the vine's tendrils: each digit a tendril curling into a numeral, with leaves budding along it (vine-script letterforms: thick-to-thin stems, spiral terminals). The rainbow frog in round glasses climbs the vine (big enough to be a character), resting on leaves. Always alive: leaves flutter in a breeze, the stalk sways as one spring-like body, dew drops slide and sparkle, a butterfly or two, sun or moon and sky gradient by the real time of day along the tall tower. Minute turn: the changing digit's tendril withers, curls up and drops its leaves (which flutter down the tower), and a new shoot grows out and curls into the new digit, leaves unfurling (growth is a beautiful, smooth transition). Hour: the vine blossoms in a wave from bottom to top, the flowers burst into petals and butterflies, and the frog reaches a new cloud.

Folding box. Five panels in a plus are the unfolded net of an open box (a lid-less cube): the centre panel is the bottom, the four arms are the four sides. Each arm carries one digit, printed on the 'cardboard' or lit as a screen face, oriented so all four read upright from the front. The material and world are yours to choose (a wooden puzzle box, a paper toy, a jewellery box, a holographic cube); the centre shows something alive (seconds, a creature living in the box, a mechanism). Always alive. Minute turn: the changing digit's side flap folds up out of the plane in real 3D perspective (rotating about its hinge on the seam to the centre panel, foreshortening and shading as it turns), swaps its face and folds back down. Hour: the whole net folds itself up into a closed 3D box that spins (true 3D, smooth), with the hour shown on its sides as it turns, then unfolds again. The assembly's own shape is the idea: use it.

Platformer level. Three panels in an L (a tall left column and a long bottom row) are one side-view level of a 16-bit-style platformer: the tall arm a tower or cliff to climb, the bottom arm a run along the ground. The level's own geometry spells the time: platforms, brick blocks, pipes, ladders and coins arranged into big numerals (design a 'level-design' font). The hero is the owner's rainbow frog in round glasses (12+ px, original character), which speedruns the level all the time with real platformer physics (acceleration, jump arcs, coyote time), wall-jumps up the tall arm and slides down. Enemies patrol, coins spin, parallax background. Minute turn: the frog bonks the changing digit's blocks from below, they break or flip, and new blocks pop into the new digit with a springy bounce. Hour: a boss appears or a flagpole at the end with a fireworks counter showing the hour. A game the owner would watch for minutes.

Fireworks night. A 128x128 night sky over water and a skyline silhouette. The time is lancework: a set piece, the firework frames that burn lettering in sputtering fire (lance letterforms: rows of individual lances, each a bright flickering spark with a tiny smoke puff, designed for this grid). The lancework burns steadily and alive: sparks flicker, drips fall, smoke drifts across and is lit from below, reflections dance on the water. Constant aerial life: a shell now and then (peony, willow, crossette, palm) with real particle physics: drag, gravity, glitter, fading trails. Minute turn: a fuse flame runs along the changing digit, its lances burn out one by one in smoke, and a new fuse ignites the new digit lance by lance along its strokes. Hour: a full finale: shells bursting in the hour's colour, a Catherine wheel, a crackling mine; the time stays readable throughout. Pure light on black: this panel's best trick.

Liquid metal. A 128x128 tray of mercury (or chrome T-1000 liquid) under a studio light: the digits are raised blobs of liquid metal, with a real environment-mapped reflection (a softbox highlight, a window, the room), surface tension rounding every edge, tiny ripples crossing them. Shade it as a heightfield: an SDF of the digits blurred into a smooth height, normals from its gradient, then reflections from a designed environment map: cheap and photoreal. Always alive: slow ripples, a wobble with the seconds, droplets that bead and merge. Minute turn: the changing digit melts back into the pool, flows sideways as a liquid bulge, and rises again as the new digit (like the T-1000 reforming), with a ring wave. Hour: the whole tray churns into one pool, the light moves, and the four digits rise again in sequence. The reflections are the wow: design the environment map with care.

Typewriter. A 128x64 close-up of a vintage typewriter typing the time onto paper: typebars swing up from the basket and strike, the ribbon lifts, the carriage steps left after each character and returns with a ding. The numerals are real typewriter type: slab-serif, with ink spread, uneven inking, a slightly misaligned letter (design the typeface for this grid). The page scrolls up a line every minute, so the past few minutes remain on the paper above as a log, fading under the paper bail. Always alive: the cursor carriage idles, the frog typist's fingers (or just the keys) hover, a coffee steam wisp, the paper flutters; seconds as the keys typing a dot leader or dashes. Minute turn: the carriage returns, the platen rolls up the line (smooth), and the new time is typed key by key. Hour: the page is torn out and a fresh sheet is fed in, with a typed heading. Mechanical, tactile.

Deep-sea jellyfish. A 64x128 deep water column, black to deep blue, with drifting marine snow. The time is carried by bioluminescent jellyfish: comb jellies with rainbow light running down their comb rows, or moon jellies whose glowing bells and trailing tentacles shape the numerals. Real motion: bells pulse with jet propulsion (contract fast, relax slow), tentacles trail as verlet ropes, everything drifts with currents. Always alive. Minute turn: the changing digit's jelly pulses away upward into the dark and a new one rises from the depth and unfurls into the new digit (never a different number on the way). Hour: a swarm passes, everything flashes in a bioluminescent wave, an anglerfish lure drifts through. Soft glow on black.

Thermal camera. The panel is the view of an infrared camera (iron or 'inferno' false-colour palette: black, purple, red, orange, yellow, white; a temperature scale bar, a crosshair with a live temperature readout, the camera's own UI). The time is written in heat: warm finger-written numerals on a cold surface (a handwriting font of heat, soft and blooming as heat diffuses), kept warm by being retraced. Always alive: heat diffuses and cools, a cat (or the rainbow frog) walks across leaving warm pawprints that fade, a mug of tea steams in a hot plume. Minute turn: the changing digit cools away while a warm fingertip (a hot blob with a hand shape) writes the new one stroke by stroke. Hour: someone sets a hot kettle down, the scene saturates white-hot, and the time re-emerges as it cools. The palette on black GOB is the wow.

Contortionists. The four digits are rubbery circus acrobats with faces (numberfolk), each body a thick soft tube with hands and feet at the ends of its stroke, on a tiny circus stage with a spotlight. They breathe, blink, balance, wobble and look at each other. Minute turn: the changing digit contorts its own body into the new digit through real squash-and-stretch (a 9 rolls up into a 0, a 1 bends into a 2), the body length conserved, a bow at the end; never a different number on the way (keep it unreadable in the middle, not wrong). Hour: they form a human pyramid, a juggling act, or a trapeze swing across the stage, then land in place. Charm and animation craft first.

Disco. A mirror ball spins near the top (real 3D: hundreds of facets, each catching the light as it turns, with sparkling glints). Its reflections are the light spots that sweep across the walls of a dark club: and the time is written by those spots. As the ball turns, the spots glide in arcs and gather into the numerals (impossible but magic), then keep sweeping. A dance floor of lit tiles below, the rainbow frog in round glasses dancing, coloured spotlights. Always alive at 120 BPM: the floor pulses, the spots shimmer and swim. Minute turn: the ball speeds up, the changing digit's spots scatter round the room and re-gather into the new digit. Hour: strobe and a full rainbow wash, the frog does a split, then the time reassembles. Groovy, glittering, smooth.
